title: Egg Fried Rice
subtitle: Chinese-style egg fried rice ready in 10 minutes
excerpt: Day-old cooked rice stir-fried with egg, spring onions, soy sauce, and sesame oil. The fastest way to turn leftover rice into a complete meal.

recipe.sourceNotes: Egg fried rice originated in China as a practical way to use leftover rice. Cold, day-old rice works far better than freshly cooked rice: the grains have dried out slightly and are separate rather than sticky, which means they fry rather than steam in the wok. Freshly cooked rice releases too much steam and the result is clumped and wet. The technique is used across Chinese, Japanese (yakimeshi), and South-East Asian cuisines.

recipeTools.notes: Or a large, well-seasoned frying pan.

content.text: Day-old rice is essential. The grains separate easily when cold; freshly cooked rice clumps. Push the rice to one side of the wok, pour the beaten egg into the empty space, and scramble it before folding through the rice. This gives distinct pieces of egg rather than a uniform coating.

items.preparation: cooked the day before, cold from the fridge

content.text: Heat the wok over the highest heat until smoking. Add the vegetable oil and swirl to coat.

Add the garlic and white parts of the spring onions. Stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add the cold rice. Press it against the wok with a spatula and toss constantly for 2 to 3 minutes until heated through and starting to crisp at the edges.
Push the rice to one side. Pour the beaten eggs into the empty space. Scramble gently until almost set, then fold through the rice.
Add the soy sauce and sesame oil. Toss to combine. Season with a little salt if needed. Scatter with the green tops of the spring onions and serve immediately.
